sections.h2: Imports rose 12.5% in FY2025-26 while exports slipped, widening the deficit

chart.title: Device deficit widened to $6,220 million as imports outpaced exports
chart.sub: US$ million, FY2025-26 provisional, 148-code device basket.

sections.means: Imports rose 12.5% to $9,850 million while exports fell 0.5% to $3,630 million, so export coverage slipped from 42% to 37%.
sections.todo: Climb the value ladder, starting with IVD reagents and X-ray/CT cores, as the post's bottom line proposes.

sections.h2: Lab and surgical instruments carry over half of the device deficit

chart.title: Lab and surgical instruments carry the largest deficits, $1,984 and $1,596 million
chart.sub: Deficit by device family, US$ million, FY2025-26 provisional.
chart.source: DGCI&S TradeStat EIDB, fetched 5 August 2026, aggregated by HS-4 family.

sections.means: Lab and analytical instruments alone run a $1,984 million deficit at 10% coverage, the largest single gap in the basket.
sections.todo: Start localisation with lab and analytical instruments, where quality-control demand is policy-captive, as the post argues.

sections.h2: Dressings and surgical consumables are net exports; lab instruments cover 10%

chart.title: Dressings and surgical consumables export well above their imports
chart.sub: Export coverage of imports, %, FY2025-26 provisional.

sections.means: Dressings export 264% of what they import and surgical consumables 157%, while lab and analytical instruments cover only 10%.
sections.todo: Point the parts-and-accessories programmes at the ~$1.7bn component layer, since assembly-only PLI leaves those imports in place.

sections.h2: India has about 3 MRI units per million people, under half the global average of 7

chart.title: India's MRI density trails the global average of 7 per million people
chart.sub: MRI units per million population, as cited in the post.
chart.source: Figures cited in the post; no separate dataset.

sections.means: India has roughly 3 MRI units per million people against a global average of 7, with only about 2,500-3,000 scanners nationally.
sections.todo: Fund MRI localisation down to magnets and gradient coils, not stopping at scanner assembly, as the post recommends.
